annotations.note: Q326 rev SAR 28.17bn (+14% QoQ), Adj EBITDA SAR 4.75bn (+40% QoQ), net debt SAR 3.03bn ($0.81bn); FY25 FCF SAR 9.21bn.
Producer is positioned in the bottom quartile (Q1) of global production costs, preserving positive EBITDA generation across cyclical commodity troughs.
>75% of revenues billed in USD/EUR against predominantly local-currency operating expenditures, creating a structural natural FX hedge.

verdict.summary: A1/A+ IG rating is firmly anchored by 70% Saudi Aramco ownership and Saudi sovereign linkage, alongside ultra-low reported net debt (SAR 3.03bn / $0.81bn at 30-Sep-26). Q3 2026 Adj EBITDA rebounded 40% QoQ to SAR 4.75bn ($1.27bn; 9M26 ~SAR 12.4bn), though petrochemical oversupply, regional conflict supply disruptions, and $880m 1H26 dividends exceeding earnings weigh on standalone credit.

positives: 70% Saudi Aramco ownership anchors A1/A+ credit profile and sovereign-tier market access.
Conservative balance sheet: Reported net debt of just SAR 3.03bn ($0.81bn) at 30-Sep-26.
Q3 2026 sequential earnings rebound: Adj EBITDA surged 40% QoQ to SAR 4.75bn ($1.27bn); ~$950m EV disposals (Europe petchem/ETP) trim loss-making assets.
negatives: Protracted petrochemical downcycle & oversupply compressing through-cycle standalone margins (1H26 adjusted losses).
Shareholder-friendly payouts: ~$880m H1-26 distributions exceeded H1 earnings, prioritizing Aramco cash returns.
Balance-sheet definition gap between reported net debt ($0.81bn at 3Q26) and legacy repo 2024A ($6.67bn) requires reconciliation.
